# Adjudication Task — Chapter 1117

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃1117화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|오늘날, 서녕의 그 어디에서도 평화라는 단어는 찾아볼 수 없었다.
  6|
  7|동서남북. 심지어는 하늘조차도 마찬가지였다.
  8|
  9|온 사방이 비와 핏물에 잠겼고 비명과 굉음은 끊이질 않았다.
 10|
 11|그러나 단 한 곳, 동문(東門)으로부터 수백여 장 밖에 우뚝 솟아있는 언덕만큼은 예외였다.
 12|
 13|‘정말이지, 끔찍하게도 퍼붓는군.’
 14|
 15|생사가 오가는 위기에 처한 이라면 도저히 떠올릴 수 없을 생각.
 16|
 17|커다란 구멍이라도 뚫린 것일까, 싶을 정도로 굵은 빗줄기를 쉴 새 없이 쏟아 내는 하늘을 바라보던 흑의인이 문득 동쪽으로 고개를 돌렸다.
 18|
 19|쏴아아아.
 20|
 21|짙게 내려앉은 어둠 속, 폭풍우와도 같은 거센 바람에 휩쓸려 출렁이는 물결.
 22|
 23|며칠간 단 한시도 쉬지 않고 계속된 유례없는 폭우로 인해, 제법 원만한 평지였던 그곳은 어느새 강이라도 불러도 이상하지 않을 정도로 변해 있었다.
 24|
 25|물론, 정작 흑의인이 확인하고자 했던 것은 따로 있었지만.
 26|
 27|“놈들은?”
 28|
 29|곁에 있던 동료가 불쑥 던진 물음에, 흑의인이 대답했다.
 30|
 31|“아직.”
 32|
 33|“예상보다 늦는군. 지금쯤이면 충분히 도착할 때도 되었는데.”
 34|
 35|“시간을 지킬 만큼 근면한 놈들이었다면 왜 도적질이나 하고 살겠나.”
 36|
 37|깊게 눌러쓴 흑의 아래, 낮은 웃음소리로 동의를 표한 동료가 말을 이었다.
 38|
 39|“하지만 이 정도까지 멍청할 줄은 몰랐어. 비록 근본도 없는 도적놈들이라 해도, 감히 맹(盟)을 자처할 정도라면 어느 정도의 수완이나 눈치쯤은 있을 줄 알았지.”
 40|
 41|“글쎄, 어쩌면 나름대로 머리를 굴린 결과일지도.”
 42|
 43|“무슨 뜻인가?”
 44|
 45|“제아무리 멍청한 종자들이라 해도 화살받이로 쓰이리라는 것쯤은 짐작했을 걸세. 저들 중 대부분은 도적 나부랭이에 불과하지만, 그 수괴(首魁)인 해상왕과 녹림투왕은 제법 머리를 굴릴 줄 알거든.”
 46|
 47|“놈들이 피해를 최소화하기 위해 일부러 늑장을 부리고 있다?”
 48|
 49|“날씨가 험해진 탓도 있겠지만, 가능성은 충분하지.”
 50|
 51|“무려 일만에 달하는 아군이 그 도적놈들을 감시하고 있을 텐데도?”
 52|
 53|“누가 알겠나. 제아무리 눈을 부릅뜨고 있어도 장강수로맹의 물귀신들이 작정하고 수작을 부린다면야.”
 54|
 55|“허, 만약 그게 사실이라면 멍청한 정도가 아니라 구제불능인데.”
 56|
 57|혀를 차는 동료의 모습에 흑의인이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 58|
 59|비록 조금 전의 대화에서 직접적으로 언급하지는 않았지만, 한 번 시작되면 뒤가 없이 날뛰는 혈주(血主)의 잔인성은 암천 내에서도 모르는 이가 없을 정도.
 60|
 61|만약 장강수로맹과 녹림맹의 연합군이 모든 전투가 끝난 후에야 뒤늦게 도착한다면…….
 62|
 63|‘오늘 이후부터 중원의 강산(江山)이 깨끗해지겠지. 도적놈들 따위는 털끝 하나 찾아볼 수 없을 만큼.’
 64|
 65|그러나 그런 그들에게도 아직 살아남을 기회는 있었다.
 66|
 67|계획에 따라 동문이 열리기 전에 때맞춰 도착하기만 한다면, 최소한의 공이라도 세워 체면을 지킨다면 그 질긴 명줄을 조금이라도 더 연장시킬 수 있을 것이다.
 68|
 69|물론, 그 또한 어디까지나 혈주의 기분에 따라 달라지겠지만.
 70|
 71|‘살고 싶다면 젖 먹던 힘까지 쥐어 짜내어 노를 젓거라. 그래야 피차 피곤하지 않을 테니.’
 72|
 73|저 멀리 한창 전투가 벌어지고 있는 동문을 바라보며, 흑의인은 내심 중얼거렸다.
 74|
 75|한낱 도적놈들의 생사 따위가 무슨 상관이겠느냐마는, 암천 내에서 이른바 강시술사(僵尸術士)로 분류되는 그에게는 상당히 중요한 문제였다.
 76|
 77|흑의인의 역할은 전장에서 싸우는 병사가 아니라, 전장에 널브러진 시체를 치우는 운반조에 가까웠으니까.
 78|
 79|그리고 과도한 업무량을 걱정하는 그의 마음과는 반대로, 동문을 둘러싸고 일진일퇴(一進一退)를 거듭하던 전투의 흐름은 급격하게 뒤바뀌고 있었다.
 80|
 81|콰아아앙!
 82|
 83|불현듯 울려 퍼지는 굉음.
 84|
 85|빗소리는 물론 때때로 내리치던 천둥마저 집어삼킨 그 커다란 소음에, 흑의인과 그 동료는 눈을 크게 떴다.
 86|
 87|그와 동시에 그들의 시야에 들어온 것은, 폭발하는 섬광과 함께 무너지는 성벽의 상단이었다.
 88|
 89|“저건…….”
 90|
 91|흑의인이 신음처럼 뇌까렸다.
 92|
 93|비록 찰나였지만, 확신할 수 있었다.
 94|
 95|지금 이 순간에도 쉴 새 없이 성벽 위에서 번뜩이고 있는 저 섬광이, 강기(罡氣)라 불리는 파괴적인 기운이라는 것을.
 96|
 97|‘왜지? 일부러 맹공을 퍼붓지도 않았는데 청허자가 어째서.’
 98|
 99|문득 곤륜파 장문인의 존재가 뇌리를 스쳤지만, 흑의인은 이내 고개를 가로저을 수밖에 없었다.
100|
101|퍼엉! 구구구궁!
102|
103|재차 터져 나오는 아득한 섬광.
104|
105|그것에 담긴 빛은, 도무지 도가(道家)의 무공으로부터 비롯되었다고 말할 수 없을 만큼 희뿌옇고 불길했으니.
106|
107|“흑귀(黑鬼)도 아닐세. 놈들은 아직 명령대로 제자리를 지키고 있어.”
108|
109|때마침 들려온 동료의 말은 사실이었다.
110|
111|두 기의 흑귀는 혈주의 지시에 따라, 일부러 투입하지 않은 상당수의 병력을 거느린 채 성벽 앞 전장에 대기 중이었으니까.
112|
113|“그렇다는 건.”
114|
115|흑의인은 문득 말을 멈췄다.
116|
117|저 강기의 주인이 흑귀도, 청허자도 아니라면 남은 것은 하나뿐이다.
118|
119|간자(間者).
120|
121|오랜 세월에 걸쳐 곤륜파에 심어두었던 간자들이 마침내 행동을 개시한 것이다.
122|
123|그것도 계획되었던 시점보다도 한발 앞서서.
124|
125|“어떻게 하지?”
126|
127|동료의 물음에 흑의인은 입술을 깨물었다.
128|
129|그로서는 참으로 빌어먹을 일이 아닐 수 없었다.
130|
131|지금쯤 전장에 도착했어야 할 장강수로맹과 녹림맹 연합군은 아직까지도 기약이 없고, 그에 맞춰 동문을 열었어야 할 간자들은 때아닌 교전을 벌이고 있다니.
132|
133|설상가상으로 그들의 직속상관이라 할 수 있는 마삼보마저 오늘 이 자리에 없었으니, 결국 흑의인이 직접 판단하고 선택할 수밖에 없었다.
134|
135|그것도 아주 신속하게.
136|
137|그리고 마치 영원처럼 느껴지는 짧은 시간 속, 수많은 갈등에 사로잡힌 채 동문을 응시하던 흑의인은 불현듯 눈을 부릅떴다.
138|
139|철컥. 그그그긍!
140|
141|육중한 마찰음과 함께 천천히 움직이기 시작한 철교(鐵橋).
142|
143|성문 앞 해자(垓字)와 연결된 그 거대한 다리가, 마치 한 줄기의 빛처럼 내려오고 있었다.
144|
145|‘철교는 성문과 이어져 있고, 따라서 반드시 내부에서만 작동시킬 수 있다.’
146|
147|그렇다면 저 광경은 곤륜파에 심어둔 간자들이 내부에서 성문을 열고 있다는 명백한 증거이자 절호의 기회.
148|
149|더 이상의 고민은, 흑의인에게 있어 무의미했다.
150|
151|“명하노니, 부름에 답하라!”
152|
153|흑의인이 외침과 동시에 허리춤에 꽂혀있던 요령(妖鈴)을 꺼내 힘차게 떨쳤다.
154|
155|우우웅.
156|
157|음산한 소리와 함께 바람을 타고 뻗어 나가는 파장.
158|
159|그와 동시에 지금껏 그들이 서 있던 언덕이, 아니 빗줄기와 혼란에 가려져 언덕이라고 착각할 수밖에 없었던 거대한 살덩어리들이 그 강렬한 파장에 응답했다.
160|
161|드드드득!
162|
163|지진이라도 일어난 것처럼 땅이 뒤흔들리고. 빗물과 흙에 가려져 있던 끔찍한 시취(屍臭)가 피어오른다.
164|
165|쿠웅, 쿠우우웅!
166|
167|전신에 치덕치덕 바른 진흙을 떨치고, 아름드리나무와도 같은 팔다리로 우뚝 선 괴물의 숫자는 도합 일천.
168|
169|그중 하나의 어깨에 걸터앉은 흑의인이 다시 한번 요령을 흔들며 속삭였다.
170|
171|“모조리 쓸어버려라.”
172|
173|그 순간.
174|
175|- 콰우우우우우!
176|
177|그 체격에 걸맞는 거대한 포효와 함께, 일천에 달하는 괴물들이 파도처럼 전장을 향해 쏟아졌다.
178|
179|두두두두두!
180|
181|황하(黃河)가 범람한다면 이런 광경일까.
182|
183|누구도 막을 수 없을 정도로 흉포한 기세로 들이닥치는 괴물들을 발견한 성벽 위에서 뒤늦게 비명이 터져 나왔지만, 그들이 상대해야 할 적은 그뿐만이 아니었다.
184|
185|
186|
187|- 전. 군.
188|
189|- 돌. 격. 하. 라.
190|
191|
192|
193|칠흑색 갑주 아래로 흘러나오는 낮은 음성.
194|
195|그와 동시에, 때를 기다리고 있던 두 기의 흑귀가 쏘아졌다.
196|
197|쐐애애액!
198|
199|새하얀 뼈를 드러낸 유령마가 바람처럼 공간을 가로지르고, 물경 수천에 달하는 광신도들이 그 뒤를 따라 돌격한다.
200|
201|전장을 뒤흔드는 외침과 함께.
202|
203|
204|
205|- 천상천하! 만마앙복!
206|
207|- 천주께서 우리와 함께하신다!
208|
209|
210|
211|등 뒤에서 울려 퍼지는 그 거대한 함성에, 흑의인은 일순간 등줄기를 타고 솟구치는 짜릿한 전율을 느꼈다.
212|
213|처음의 계획에서 다소 어긋나긴 했으나, 이제 그런 사소한 문제점 따위는 아무런 상관도 없었다.
214|
215|자신의 뒤에는 말 그대로의 천군만마(千軍萬馬)가 있었고, 어느덧 절반 가까이 내려온 철교의 뒤에는…….
216|
217|‘보인다!’
218|
219|확실했다.
220|
221|결코 헛것 따위가 아니었다.
222|
223|쇠사슬로 연결되어 있던 철교가 내려감에 따라 서서히 열리기 시작한 거대한 철문이, 환희에 물든 흑의인의 눈동자에 선명히 비치고 있었다.
224|
225|츠츠츠츠!
226|
227|확신에 찬 두 강시술사의 손짓을 따라 요령이 춤추듯 흔들리자, 한계치까지 속도를 끌어올린 괴물들이 동문을 향해 쏘아졌다.
228|
229|‘할 수 있다.’
230|
231|느려진 시간 속, 흑의인은 숨을 삼킨 채 시야에 들어온 전장의 상황을 바라보았다.
232|
233|굉음과 먼지로 뒤덮인 성벽 위에서는 쉴 새 없이 섬광이 번뜩이고, 절반도 넘게 내려온 철교는 해자를 덮고 있다.
234|
235|이제 남아 있는 거리는, 고작 일백여 장.
236|
237|‘더, 더 빨리……!’
238|
239|선두에서 쏘아지는 괴물들의 걸음 소리가 천둥처럼 울려 퍼지고, 두 기의 흑귀를 태운 채 그 옆에서 나란히 내달리는 유령마의 움직임은 흡사 귀신의 그것과도 같았다.
240|
241|쉬이이익!
242|
243|세찬 바람이 전신을 휘감는다. 시시각각 좁혀지는 거리에 따라 가슴이 두방망이질 친다.
244|
245|일백여 장이 반으로.
246|
247|또 그 반으로.
248|
249|그리고 마침내.
250|
251|그그그긍. 쿠웅!
252|
253|길고 단단한 철교가 해자 위로 내려앉은 순간.
254|
255|콰아앙!
256|
257|가장 먼저 철교를 가로지른 두 기의 흑귀를 선두로, 일천의 괴물들이 하나의 거대한 송곳처럼 활짝 열린 성문을 향해 쏟아졌다.
258|
259|콰드드드드득!
260|
261|무시무시한 굉음과 함께 피어오르는 흙먼지 속, 마침내 동문이라는 둑을 허물어트린 흑의인과 그 동료는 참았던 숨을 토해 냈다.
262|
263|해냈다. 그들만의 힘으로.
264|
265|이는 그 누구도 이견을 제시할 수 없을 만큼 완벽한 성공인 동시에, 실로 혁혁한 전공(戰功)이었다.

“But I didn’t think they’d be this stupid. They may be rootless bandits, but if they dare call themselves an Alliance, I thought they’d have at least a little skill or sense.”

[P20]
“Maybe this is the result of them thinking things through, in their own way.”

[P21]
“What do you mean?”

[P22]
“Even fools can guess when they’re being used as cannon fodder. Most of them are petty bandits, but their leaders—the Seafaring King and the Green Forest Battle King—know how to use their heads.”

[P23]
“So they’re deliberately dragging their feet to minimize their losses?”

[P24]
“The weather’s gotten worse, too, but it’s certainly possible.”

[P25]
“Even with nearly ten thousand of our people watching those bandits?”

[P26]
“Who knows? Those water ghosts of the Yangtze River Channel League might pull something if they put their minds to it, no matter how closely we watch.”

[P27]
“Ha. If that’s true, they’re not just stupid. They’re beyond saving.”

[P28]
The black-robed man nodded as his companion clicked his tongue.

[P29]
Neither had said it outright, but everyone in Dark Heaven knew how cruel the Blood Lord could be once he began rampaging with no thought for what came after.

[P30]
If the combined forces of the Yangtze River Channel League and the Green Forest Alliance arrived only after the fighting was over…

[P31]
*After today, the Central Plains will be clean. You won’t find so much as a hair from one of those bandits.*

[P32]
But they still had a chance to survive.

[P33]
If they arrived in time, before the East Gate opened as planned, and earned even a little credit to save face, they might extend their stubborn lives a while longer.

[P34]
Of course, that depended on the Blood Lord’s mood.

[P35]
*If you want to live, row with every last bit of strength you’ve got. It’ll save us both a headache.*

[P36]
The black-robed man looked toward the East Gate, where the battle was raging.

[P37]
What did he care whether a bunch of bandits lived or died? But for someone Dark Heaven classified as a corpse sorcerer, it mattered quite a lot.

[P38]
His role was less that of a soldier fighting on the battlefield than a member of the crew hauling away the corpses scattered across it.

[P39]
And while he worried about the extra work, the battle around the East Gate, which had been seesawing back and forth, suddenly took a sharp turn.

[P40]
BOOOOM!

[P41]
A deafening crash rang out.

[P42]
It swallowed the sound of the rain and even the occasional thunder. The black-robed man and his companion stared wide-eyed.

[P43]
The top of the fortress wall was collapsing amid a burst of light.

[P44]
“What was that…?”

[P45]
The black-robed man’s words came out as a groan.

[P46]
The flash had lasted only an instant, but he was sure. The destructive energy still flaring across the wall was Force.

[P47]
*Why? We haven’t even pressed the attack. Why would Cheongheoja…?*

[P48]
The Kunlun Sect Leader came to mind, but the black-robed man shook his head.

[P49]
POP! RUMMMBLE!

[P50]
Another distant flash burst into view. Its pale, ominous light could hardly have come from Daoist martial arts.

[P51]
“It’s not the Black Ghosts, either. They’re still holding their positions as ordered.”

[P52]
His companion was right.

[P53]
The two Black Ghosts were waiting on the battlefield in front of the wall, along with a considerable number of troops the Blood Lord had deliberately held back.

[P54]
“Which means…”

[P55]
The black-robed man stopped.

[P56]
If that Force belonged to neither Cheongheoja nor a Black Ghost, there was only one possibility.

[P57]
Spies.

[P58]
The spies they had planted in the Kunlun Sect over many years had finally made their move—a step ahead of schedule.

[P59]
“What do we do?”

[P60]
The black-robed man bit his lip.

[P61]
It was a real pain in the ass.

[P62]
The combined forces of the Yangtze River Channel League and the Green Forest Alliance should have reached the battlefield by now, but there was still no sign of them. Meanwhile, the spies who were supposed to open the East Gate when they arrived were caught up in an unexpected fight.

[P63]
To make matters worse, Ma Sanbao—effectively their direct superior—wasn’t there today. The black-robed man would have to make the call himself.

[P64]
And fast.

[P65]
He stared at the East Gate, torn between his options. The moment was brief, though it felt like an eternity. Then his eyes widened.

[P66]
CLANK. GRRRRNNG!

[P67]
The iron bridge began to move with a heavy grinding sound.

[P68]
The massive bridge was lowering toward the moat in front of the gate, like a ray of light cutting through the darkness.

[P69]
*The bridge is connected to the gate. It can only be operated from inside.*

[P70]
It was clear proof that the spies planted in the Kunlun Sect were opening the gate—and the perfect opportunity.

[P71]
There was no point hesitating any longer.

[P72]
“I command you: answer the call!”

[P73]
The black-robed man pulled the ritual bell from his belt and shook it hard.

[P74]
Wooooong.

[P75]
A sinister sound carried on the wind, its vibrations spreading outward.

[P76]
The hill they had been standing on answered. Or rather, the enormous masses of flesh that the rain and chaos had made look like a hill did.

[P77]
GRRRRKK!

[P78]
The ground shook as if an earthquake had struck. A horrible corpse stench rose through the rain and mud.

[P79]
BOOM. BOOOOM!

[P80]
The monsters shook off the mud plastered over their bodies and stood on limbs as thick as great trees. There were a thousand in all.

[P81]
Perched on one monster’s shoulder, the black-robed man shook his ritual bell again and whispered, “Wipe them all out.”

[P82]
At that instant—

[P83]
—KROOOAAAR!

[P84]
With roars to match their immense bodies, a thousand monsters surged toward the battlefield like a wave.

[P85]
THUDDUDDUDDUD!

[P86]
Was this what the Yellow River would look like in flood?

[P87]
Screams rose belatedly from the wall as the defenders spotted the monsters bearing down on them with unstoppable momentum. But those weren’t the only enemies they had to face.

[P88]
—All. Troops.

[P89]
—Charge.

[P90]
A low voice emerged from beneath black armor.

[P91]
At the same time, the two Black Ghosts who had been waiting sprang forward.

[P92]
SHWOOOSH!

[P93]
A ghost horse, its white bones exposed, raced ahead like the wind. Several thousand fanatics charged behind it, their cries shaking the battlefield.

[P94]
—Heaven above and earth below! Let ten thousand demons bow in homage!

[P95]
—The Lord of Heaven is with us!

[P96]
The immense shouts behind him sent a thrilling shiver up the black-robed man’s spine.

[P97]
Things had strayed a little from the original plan, but those minor setbacks no longer mattered.

[P98]
He had an army at his back. And beyond the iron bridge, which had descended nearly halfway…

[P99]
*I see it!*

[P100]
There was no doubt. He wasn’t seeing things.

[P101]
As the bridge lowered on its chains, the enormous iron gate began to open. He could see it clearly.

[P102]
Tss-tss-tss-tss!

[P103]
The two corpse sorcerers shook their ritual bells with confident sweeps of their hands. The monsters pushed themselves to their limit and shot toward the East Gate.

[P104]
*We can do this.*

[P105]
Time seemed to slow. The black-robed man held his breath and watched the battlefield.

[P106]
Flashes burst without pause atop the wall amid crashes and dust. The bridge, now more than halfway down, was stretching over the moat.

[P107]
Only a little over a hundred jang remained.

[P108]
*Faster. Faster…!*

[P109]
The leading monsters’ footsteps thundered across the ground. Beside them, the ghost horse carrying the two Black Ghosts galloped with uncanny speed.

[P110]
Whoooosh!

[P111]
A fierce wind wrapped around the black-robed man. His heart pounded as the distance shrank.

[P112]
A little over a hundred jang became half that.

[P113]
Then half again.

[P114]
And at last—

[P115]
GRRRNNG. BOOM!

[P116]
The long, sturdy iron bridge settled over the moat.

[P117]
BOOOOM!

[P118]
The two Black Ghosts crossed first. Behind them, a thousand monsters surged toward the wide-open gate like one enormous spear.

[P119]
KRRRRRUNCH!

[P120]
A terrifying crash sent dust billowing into the air. The black-robed man and his companion had finally broken through the barrier of the East Gate, and they let out the breaths they had been holding.

[P121]
They had done it. By their own strength.

[P122]
No one could dispute their success—or the magnitude of their feat.

[P123]
Even the merciless Blood Lord would have to acknowledge it.

[P124]
For that moment, at least, both men could rejoice.

[P125]
SHWING—BOOM!

[P126]
Then a dazzling flash of Force flew in from somewhere and shattered the thick chain connecting the gate and the iron bridge.

[P127]
CLANK. RRRRRK!

[P128]
It happened too quickly for anyone to react.

[P129]
“……!”

[P130]
“……!”

[P131]
The two corpse sorcerers stared blankly as the heavy gate began to close. Beyond the settling dust, a hazy figure came into view.

[P132]
SPLASH. SPLASH.

[P133]
Staggering steps. A robe soaked in blood.

[P134]
Then the middle-aged man’s face emerged, his eyes glowing red as if to prove he had committed a forbidden act.

[P135]
“……You.”

[P136]
The black-robed man had barely spoken when—

[P137]
Slice!

[P138]
A streak of light cut through the dust and across the middle-aged man’s—no, Hak Su’s—neck.

[P139]
A voice rang out, thick with sorrow and anger.

[P140]
“By the solemn rules of the Great Kunlun Sect, I execute those who have sinned against our sect.”

[P141]
THUD. FWOOSH.

[P142]
The headless body collapsed, and the dust cloud parted.

[P143]
Only then did the two corpse sorcerers see their surroundings clearly. Only then did they understand.

[P144]
The spies hadn’t lowered the bridge and opened the gate. The defenders of the East Gate had.

[P145]
*A trap…!*

[P146]
The realization struck like lightning.

[P147]
But the shock lasted only a moment. There were fewer than three thousand defenders, and Cheongheoja looked exhausted. The black-robed man’s lips twisted into a grin.

[P148]
“You dare try such a shoddy trick?”

[P149]
It was a trap, but it was hardly enough.

[P150]
The gate had shut out the fanatics following them, but their strongest forces—the Black Ghosts and the monsters—were already inside.

[P151]
“Did you think this would stop us?”

[P152]
A young man standing beside Cheongheoja answered his scornful question.

[P153]
“Why not? We’ve been through a whole lot worse. Right, everyone?”

[P154]
The black-robed man frowned at him. There was something about the young man’s face that made him want to torment him.

[P155]
Just then, a young beggar with grime streaming down his face spoke up.

[P156]
“Quit saying ‘beggar’ every other word. You’ll hurt the beggar’s feelings.”

[P157]
“Who the hell are you…?”

[P158]
“Honestly, we end up in situations like this every time. I can’t even figure out how much extra pay we’re owed anymore.”

[P159]
A cold-faced young man cut him off. Then a clear voice, utterly at odds with the mood, rang out.

[P160]
“But we always made it through. Together.”

[P161]
“True, but this time is different. The most important person isn’t here.”

[P162]
“Right. Taishan wants to eat Pavilion Master. Old Man Nam, too.”

[P163]
“Taishan. You mean you miss them, not that you want to eat them.”

[P164]
“Oh. Got mixed up. My lord is smart, as expected.”

[P165]
“Not bad. Still, not as smart as me.”

[P166]
Young men and women the corpse sorcerers had never seen before. A hulking man who looked none too bright. A wild-haired eccentric.

[P167]
Faced with the bizarre sight, the two sorcerers couldn’t think of anything to ask.

[P168]
More precisely, they didn’t think it was worth asking.

[P169]
“Wipe them all out.”

[P170]
The ritual bell began to move with his quiet command.

[P171]
Boooooo!

[P172]
A horn sounded in the distance, and everyone at the East Gate stopped moving.

[P173]
For some, that sound meant hope. For others, utter despair.

[P174]
“The Yangtze River Channel League…”

[P175]
Someone’s low groan hung heavily in the air.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P52]
His companion was right.

[P53]
The two Black Ghosts were waiting on the battlefield in front of the wall, along with a considerable number of troops the Blood Lord had deliberately held back.

[P54]
“Which means…”

[P55]
The black-robed man stopped.

[P56]
If that Force belonged to neither Cheongheoja nor a Black Ghost, there was only one possibility.

[P57]
Spies.

[P58]
The spies they had planted in the Kunlun Sect over many years had finally made their move—a step ahead of schedule.

[P59]
“What do we do?”

[P60]
The black-robed man bit his lip.

[P61]
It was a real pain in the ass.

[P62]
The combined forces of the Yangtze River Channel League and the Green Forest Alliance should have reached the battlefield by now, but there was still no sign of them. Meanwhile, the spies who were supposed to open the East Gate when they arrived were caught up in an unexpected fight.

[P63]
To make matters worse, Ma Sanbao—effectively their direct superior—wasn’t there today. The black-robed man would have to make the call himself.

[P64]
And fast.

[P65]
He stared at the East Gate, torn between his options. The moment was brief, though it felt like an eternity. Then his eyes widened.

[P66]
CLANK. GRRRRNNG!

[P67]
The iron bridge began to move with a heavy grinding sound.

[P68]
The massive bridge was lowering toward the moat in front of the gate, like a ray of light cutting through the darkness.

[P69]
*The bridge is connected to the gate. It can only be operated from inside.*

[P70]
It was clear proof that the spies planted in the Kunlun Sect were opening the gate—and the perfect opportunity.

[P71]
There was no point hesitating any longer.

[P72]
“I command you: answer the call!”

[P73]
The black-robed man pulled the ritual bell from his belt and shook it hard.

[P74]
Wooooong.

[P75]
A sinister sound carried on the wind, its vibrations spreading outward.

[P76]
The hill they had been standing on answered. Or rather, the enormous masses of flesh that the rain and chaos had made look like a hill did.

[P77]
GRRRRKK!

[P78]
The ground shook as if an earthquake had struck. A horrible corpse stench rose through the rain and mud.

[P79]
BOOM. BOOOOM!

[P80]
The monsters shook off the mud plastered over their bodies and stood on limbs as thick as great trees. There were a thousand in all.

[P81]
Perched on one monster’s shoulder, the black-robed man shook his ritual bell again and whispered, “Wipe them all out.”

[P82]
At that instant—

[P83]
—KROOOAAAR!

[P84]
With roars to match their immense bodies, a thousand monsters surged toward the battlefield like a wave.

[P85]
THUDDUDDUDDUD!

[P86]
Was this what the Yellow River would look like in flood?

[P87]
Screams rose belatedly from the wall as the defenders spotted the monsters bearing down on them with unstoppable momentum. But those weren’t the only enemies they had to face.

[P88]
—All. Troops.

[P89]
—Charge.

[P90]
A low voice emerged from beneath black armor.

[P91]
At the same time, the two Black Ghosts who had been waiting sprang forward.

[P92]
SHWOOOSH!

[P93]
A ghost horse, its white bones exposed, raced ahead like the wind. Several thousand fanatics charged behind it, their cries shaking the battlefield.

[P94]
—Heaven above and earth below! Let ten thousand demons bow in homage!

[P95]
—The Lord of Heaven is with us!

[P96]
The immense shouts behind him sent a thrilling shiver up the black-robed man’s spine.

[P97]
Things had strayed a little from the original plan, but those minor setbacks no longer mattered.

[P98]
He had an army at his back. And beyond the iron bridge, which had descended nearly halfway…

[P99]
*I see it!*

[P100]
There was no doubt. He wasn’t seeing things.

[P101]
As the bridge lowered on its chains, the enormous iron gate began to open. He could see it clearly.

[P102]
Tss-tss-tss-tss!

[P103]
The two corpse sorcerers shook their ritual bells with confident sweeps of their hands. The monsters pushed themselves to their limit and shot toward the East Gate.

[P104]
*We can do this.*

[P105]
Time seemed to slow. The black-robed man held his breath and watched the battlefield.

[P106]
Flashes burst without pause atop the wall amid crashes and dust. The bridge, now more than halfway down, was stretching over the moat.

[P107]
Only a little over a hundred jang remained.

[P108]
*Faster. Faster…!*

[P109]
The leading monsters’ footsteps thundered across the ground. Beside them, the ghost horse carrying the two Black Ghosts galloped with uncanny speed.

[P110]
Whoooosh!

[P111]
A fierce wind wrapped around the black-robed man. His heart pounded as the distance shrank.

[P112]
A little over a hundred jang became half that.

[P113]
Then half again.

[P114]
And at last—

[P115]
GRRRNNG. BOOM!

[P116]
The long, sturdy iron bridge settled over the moat.

[P117]
BOOOOM!

[P118]
The two Black Ghosts crossed first. Behind them, a thousand monsters surged toward the wide-open gate like one enormous spear.

[P119]
KRRRRRUNCH!

[P120]
A terrifying crash sent dust billowing into the air. The black-robed man and his companion had finally broken through the barrier of the East Gate, and they let out the breaths they had been holding.

[P121]
They had done it. By their own strength.

[P122]
No one could dispute their success—or the magnitude of their feat.

[P123]
Even the merciless Blood Lord would have to acknowledge it.

[P124]
For that moment, at least, both men could rejoice.

[P125]
SHWING—BOOM!

[P126]
Then a dazzling flash of Force flew in from somewhere and shattered the thick chain connecting the gate and the iron bridge.

[P127]
CLANK. RRRRRK!

[P128]
It happened too quickly for anyone to react.

[P129]
“……!”

[P130]
“……!”

[P131]
The two corpse sorcerers stared blankly as the heavy gate began to close. Beyond the settling dust, a hazy figure came into view.

[P132]
SPLASH. SPLASH.

[P133]
Staggering steps. A robe soaked in blood.

[P134]
Then the middle-aged man’s face emerged, his eyes glowing red as if to prove he had committed a forbidden act.

[P135]
“……You.”

[P136]
The black-robed man had barely spoken when—

[P137]
Slice!

[P138]
A streak of light cut through the dust and across the middle-aged man’s—no, Hak Su’s—neck.

[P139]
A voice rang out, thick with sorrow and anger.

[P140]
“By the solemn rules of the Great Kunlun Sect, I execute those who have sinned against our sect.”

[P141]
THUD. FWOOSH.

[P142]
The headless body collapsed, and the dust cloud parted.

[P143]
Only then did the two corpse sorcerers see their surroundings clearly. Only then did they understand.

[P144]
The spies hadn’t lowered the bridge and opened the gate. The defenders of the East Gate had.

[P145]
*A trap…!*

[P146]
The realization struck like lightning.

[P147]
But the shock lasted only a moment. There were fewer than three thousand defenders, and Cheongheoja looked exhausted. The black-robed man’s lips twisted into a grin.

[P148]
“You dare try such a shoddy trick?”

[P149]
It was a trap, but it was hardly enough.

[P150]
The gate had shut out the fanatics following them, but their strongest forces—the Black Ghosts and the monsters—were already inside.

[P151]
“Did you think this would stop us?”

[P152]
A young man standing beside Cheongheoja answered his scornful question.

[P153]
“Why not? We’ve been through a whole lot worse. Right, everyone?”

[P154]
The black-robed man frowned at him. There was something about the young man’s face that made him want to torment him.

[P155]
Just then, a young beggar with grime streaming down his face spoke up.

[P156]
“Quit saying ‘beggar’ every other word. You’ll hurt the beggar’s feelings.”

[P157]
“Who the hell are you…?”

[P158]
“Honestly, we end up in situations like this every time. I can’t even figure out how much extra pay we’re owed anymore.”

[P159]
A cold-faced young man cut him off. Then a clear voice, utterly at odds with the mood, rang out.

[P160]
“But we always made it through. Together.”

[P161]
“True, but this time is different. The most important person isn’t here.”

[P162]
“Right. Taishan wants to eat Pavilion Master. Old Man Nam, too.”

[P163]
“Taishan. You mean you miss them, not that you want to eat them.”

[P164]
“Oh. Got mixed up. My lord is smart, as expected.”

[P165]
“Not bad. Still, not as smart as me.”

[P166]
Young men and women the corpse sorcerers had never seen before. A hulking man who looked none too bright. A wild-haired eccentric.

[P167]
Faced with the bizarre sight, the two sorcerers couldn’t think of anything to ask.

[P168]
More precisely, they didn’t think it was worth asking.

[P169]
“Wipe them all out.”

[P170]
The ritual bell began to move with his quiet command.

[P171]
Boooooo!

[P172]
A horn sounded in the distance, and everyone at the East Gate stopped moving.

[P173]
For some, that sound meant hope. For others, utter despair.

[P174]
“The Yangtze River Channel League…”

[P175]
Someone’s low groan hung heavily in the air.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
